Cherry]], incumbent lieutenant governor === Campaign === [[File:Betsy Devos.jpg|thumb|Dick DeVos' wife, [[Betsy DeVos|Betsy]], with a supporter at a campaign event in [[Houghton County, Michigan|Houghton County]]]] After her first election as governor in [[2002 Michigan gubernatorial election|2002]], Granholm was widely seen as a rising star in the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]]. Her popularity dropped after she took office in 2003, largely due to a weak economy and high unemployment. In August 2006, her approval rating was 47 percent.{{cite web | url=http://strategicvision.biz/political/michigan_poll_082906.htm | title=Strategic Vision Political | access-date=2006-11-09 | date=August 27, 2006 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060902045345/http://www.strategicvision.biz/political/michigan_poll_082906.htm | archive-date=September 2, 2006 }} DeVos, a multimillionaire, had developed substantial political contacts with the full participation of his wife, former [[Michigan Republican Party]] chair [[Betsy DeVos]], despite which, fully 85% of the DeVos campaign's contributions were from DeVos' inheritance.Land, Terri Lynn (Michigan Secretary of State). [http://miboecfr.nictusa.com/cgi-bin/cfr/com_det.cgi?com_id=512426 " Campaign Finance Disclosure"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081108073844/http://miboecfr.nictusa.com/cgi-bin/cfr/com_det.cgi?com_id=512426 |date=2008-11-08 }} As the 2006 election approached, the DeVos family was listed among the biggest Republican campaign contributors in Michigan.{{cite web|title=DeVoses pour millions into GOP causes |date=June 18, 2006 |access-date=2006-11-09 |work=Detroit Free Press |url=http://www.freep.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20060618/NEWS06/606180604/1008 |author=Christoff, Chris |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060627023047/http://www.freep.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=%2F20060618%2FNEWS06%2F606180604%2F1008 |archive-date=June 27, 2006 }} The DeVos campaign spent $42.5 million, at that time the most spent on a gubernatorial campaign in Michigan history. $35.5 million of that total came from DeVos' personal fortune, and was at that time the most spent personally by a Republican candidate running for governor. The Granholm campaign spent $15.7 million. The combined money spent by both campaigns made this the most expensive gubernatorial election in Michigan history. As DeVos funded his campaign himself, he was not eligible for public funds.{{cite web | url=http://www.mcfn.org/pdfs/reports/07_MCFN_Cit_Guide.pdf | title=2006 Citizen's Guide to Michigan Campaign Finance | work=Michigan Campaign Finance Network | date=18 July 2007 | access-date=18 January 2015 | archive-date=5 December 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141205140450/http://www.mcfn.org/pdfs/reports/07_MCFN_Cit_Guide.pdf | url-status=live }} The DeVos and Campbell campaigns each made the state's economy their major issue. DeVos criticized the Single Business Tax, high unemployment, and job outsourcing which occurred during Granholm's first term; Campbell assailed the $12 billion taken from Michigan's taxpayers and appropriated to the military siege of Iraq (which he calls "Duh-bya's Folly") and advocated for a local currency, independent of the U.S. dollar which he and running mate David Skrbina say is in imminent jeopardy of collapse. Granholm countered that her policies saved thousands of jobs. She also attacked DeVos's partisanship, wealth, and tenure at Alticor. One of Granholm's most prominent lines of attack was the accusation that Alticor, under DeVos's tenure, outsourced thousands of jobs to China while cutting 1,400 jobs in Michigan, a charge that the DeVos campaign and numerous media factcheckers denied. "gregcreswell.lpwm.org" (website) Campbell spent less than $1,000,http://miboecfr.nicusa.com/cfr/dumpimages/2743511.pdf {{dead link|date=August 2012}} as was the case with the Dashairya campaign.http://miboecfr.nicusa.com/cfr/dumpimages/2802601.pdf {{dead link|date=August 2012}} ===Debates=== [[File:GranDebate.jpg|thumb|left|alt=Granholm and Devos at an October 12 informal debate at the Detroit Economic Club|Granholm and Devos at an October 12 informal debate at the Detroit Economic Club]] The DeVos and Granholm campaigns agreed to three televised debates and a single joint appearance. This agreement did not include any provision for participation by third-party candidates.{{cite web | title=Agreement Governing Debates and Joint Appearances in Michigan's 2006 Gubernatorial Campaign | url=http://woodtv.triton.net/news/debate/agreement.pdf | work=[[WOOD-TV]] | access-date=January 18, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303170602/http://woodtv.triton.net/news/debate/agreement.pdf | archive-date=2016-03-03 }} Granholm and DeVos appeared together October 12 at the [[Detroit Economic Club]] in which each candidate delivered their job plans, which was described as a debate at the event itself, even if it wasn't officially designated as such.{{cite news | url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1350&dat=20061013&id=tnhhAAAAIBAJ&pg=6708,3362642 | title=Granholm, DeVos find common ground on 1 topic | work=[[Toledo Blade]] | date=October 13, 2006 | access-date=18 January 2015 | archive-date=6 October 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006122433/https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1350&dat=20061013&id=tnhhAAAAIBAJ&pg=6708,3362642 | url-status=live }} ====WKAR-TV debate==== The first debate occurred on October 2 at [[WKAR-TV]] in [[East Lansing, Michigan|East Lansing]].{{cite news | title=A Special Broadcast from WKAR | url=http://www.wkar.org/specials/debateforgovernor/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061006124328/http://wkar.org/specials/debateforgovernor/ | archive-date=October 6, 2006 | work=[[WKAR-TV]]}} Both candidates spent the hour trading charges and countercharges. ''[[Detroit News]]'' pollster Ed Sarpolus indicated that there was no clear winner in the debate, but Bill Rustem, senior vice president of the nonpartisan policy firm Public Sector Consultants in Lansing, favored Granholm.http://www.detnews.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20061003/POLITICS01/610030400 {{Dead link|date=July 2022}} The consensus of pundits Bill Ballenger, George Bullard, Kathy Barks Hoffman and Rick Albin and capital correspondent Tim Skubick, speaking on the October 6 WKAR-television program Off the Record,{{cite web |url=http://wkar.org/offtherecord/program.php?num=2007-14 |title = Off the Record |access-date=2007-09-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061006134359/https://wkar.org/offtherecord/program.php?num=2007-14 |archive-date=2006-10-06 }} was that both DeVos and Granholm emerged losers, losing 2 and 4 percentage points' support after the event. No major gaffes or zingers came out in the debate. Some of the positions were made clear on embryonic stem cell research {{cite web |url=http://www.lsj.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20061003/NEWS01/610030335/1312 |title= Lansing State Journal - Home|website=www.lsj.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061004003635/http://www.lsj.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=%2F20061003%2FNEWS01%2F610030335%2F1312 |archive-date=2006-10-04}} and abortion.{{cite web |url=http://www.theoaklandpress.com/stories/100306/loc_2006100327.shtml |title = The Oakland Press: Local News |access-date=2006-10-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061021174925/http://www.theoaklandpress.com/stories/100306/loc_2006100327.shtml |archive-date=2006-10-21 }} No major gaffes came out in the debate, but one minor zinger was made by Granholm about DeVos' investment in Alterra, a chain of nursing homes which sexually abused and neglected its patients.http://www.detnews.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20061004/POLITICS01/610040369 {{Dead link|date=July 2022}}{{cite news |url=http://www.mlive.com/news/grpress/index.ssf?%2Fbase%2Fnews-32%2F1160206504163180.xml&coll=6 |title= |newspaper=Grand Rapids Press |access-date=2006-10-08 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304050253/http://www.mlive.com/news/grpress/index.ssf?%2Fbase%2Fnews-32%2F1160206504163180.xml&coll=6 |url-status=dead }} ====WOOD-TV debate==== The second was October 10 at [[WOOD-TV]] in [[Grand Rapids, Michigan|Grand Rapids]]. DeVos was more aggressive than before, declaring that Granholm had lied about him having a controlling stake in Alterra Health Care, an elder-care company that suppressed information about the abuse of residents by its employees.{{cite web |url=http://www.mlive.com/news/grpress/index.ssf?/base/news-32/116057011613340.xml&coll=6&thispage=2 |title=Archived copy |website=www.mlive.com |access-date=22 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930153914/http://www.mlive.com/news/grpress/index.ssf?/base/news-32/116057011613340.xml&coll=6&thispage=2 |archive-date=30 September 2007 }} According to SEC filings, DeVos and his investment partners jointly owned 40% of Alterra stock totalling $173 million.{{cite web |url=http://sec.edgar-online.com/2001/04/30/0000950144-01-501321/Section9.asp |title = ALTERRA HEALTHCARE CORP Amended Annual Report (10-K/A) ITEM 12 SECURITY OWNERSHIP OF CERTAIN BENEFICIAL OWNERS AND ... |access-date=2006-10-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071001005040/http://sec.edgar-online.com/2001/04/30/0000950144-01-501321/Section9.asp |archive-date=2007-10-01 }} The chairman of Alterra's board, while a close associate of DeVos, nevertheless maintains that DeVos had no part of running the company himself.{{cite news |url=http://www.mlive.com/news/muchronicle/index.ssf?%2Fbase%2Fnews-5%2F1160059527159120.xml&coll=8&thispage=1 |title= |newspaper=Muskegon Chronicle |access-date=2006-10-12 |archive-date=2007-09-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930155014/http://www.mlive.com/news/muchronicle/index.ssf?%2Fbase%2Fnews-5%2F1160059527159120.xml&coll=8&thispage=1 |url-status=dead }} DeVos also asserted that he had convinced President Bush to set a date to meet with the three major Michigan auto companies. Granholm responded that she did not believe that was true. DeVos admitted after the debate that he misspoke; the president agreed to have a meeting at some point after the election, but did not confirm a date.{{cite web |url=http://www.ludingtondailynews.com/news.php?story_id=33320 |title=Ludington Daily News {{!}} shorelinemedia.net |access-date=2006-10-11 |archive-date=2012-02-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120205185025/http://www.ludingtondailynews.com/news.php?story_id=33320 |url-status=live }} On October 24, two weeks after this debate was held, a mid-November date was set for the meeting.http://www.detnews.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20061025/AUTO01/610250385 {{Dead link|date=July 2022}} ====WXYZ-TV debate==== The third televised debate was October 16 at [[WXYZ-TV]] in [[Southfield, Michigan|Southfield]].
